extracted.intended_audience: implementers/authors of Content MathML (software developers, spec authors, tool authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation of Content MathML operator elements and their intended semantics, syntax, qualifiers, and sample presentations for implementers and content authors. Covers unary/binary operators, calculus operators, constants, quantifiers, lambda, intervals, and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Logical Operators (not)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <not/> element represents the logical not function which takes one Boolean argument, and returns the opposite Boolean value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator appears as a unary operator in Content MathML; example: <apply><not/><ci>a</ci></apply> with sample presentation ¬a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Arithmetic Operators (factorial, abs, conjugate, arg, real, imaginary, floor, ceiling, exp, minus, root)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements represent standard unary arithmetic operations: factorial (on non-negative integers), abs (absolute value; numerically valued argument; modulus for complex), conjugate (complex conjugate), arg (angular argument of complex number), real/imaginary (real/imaginary part constructors), floor (round down to nearest integer), ceiling (round up), exp (exponential), minus (can be unary or binary), root (treated as unary with optional degree qualifier representing nth root).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions, domain expectations (e.g. factorial on non-negative integers, floor/ceiling take real numbers), notes about minus being both unary and binary and root's dual interpretation. Examples and sample presentations are provided (e.g. n!, |x|, complex conjugate notation, arg(x+iy), ⌊a⌋, e^x, unary minus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Linear Algebra Operators (determinant, transpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <determinant/> element is the unary function returning the determinant of its argument, which should be a square matrix. The <transpose/> element represents the transpose of a given matrix or vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Functional Operators (inverse, ident, domain, codomain, image, ln)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements for functions: <inverse/> constructs a generic expression for a functional inverse; <ident/> represents the identity function; <domain/> represents the function's domain; <codomain/> represents the codomain (not necessarily equal to image); <image/> denotes the image (set of values taken by the function); <ln/> is the natural logarithm function. Elements may be applied to arguments or appear alone to represent abstract operators acting on functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on contextual dependence of ident (domain/codomain depend on context). Examples show composition f ∘ f^{-1} = id, domain(f) = R, codomain(f) = Q, image(sin) = [-1,1], ln a. The elements can restrict/describe functions and their properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Set Operators (cardinality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <card/> element represents the cardinality function which takes a set argument and returns its cardinality: a non-negative integer or an infinite cardinal number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: |A| = 5 expressed as <apply><card/><ci>A</ci></apply> <cn>5</cn>. Sample presentation shows |A| = 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Elementary Operators (trigonometric, hyperbolic, inverse variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements denote standard trigonometric and hyperbolic functions and their inverses: <sin/>, <cos/>, <tan/>, <sec/>, <csc/>, <cot/>, <sinh/>, <cosh/>, <tanh/>, <sech/>, <csch/>, <coth/>, and various arc- (inverse) forms including <arcsin/>, <arccos/>, <arctan/>, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because standard interpretations vary for inverse functions, for interoperability applications evaluating such expressions should follow definitions in DLMF Chapter 4: Elementary Functions. Examples and sample presentations (sin x, sin(cos x + x^3), arcsin x or sin^{-1} x, etc.) are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unary Vector Calculus Operators (divergence, grad, curl, laplacian)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements <divergence/>, <grad/>, <curl/>, <laplacian/> represent standard vector calculus operators: divergence (takes a vector of scalar-valued functions and returns a scalar), grad (takes a scalar and returns a vector), curl (takes vector and returns vector), Laplacian (takes a vector of scalar-valued functions and returns a vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may be written with alternative notations (div f or ∇·E, grad(f) or ∇(f), curl(a) or ∇×a, ∇^2(E)). The functions defining coordinates may be defined implicitly as expressions in terms of coordinate names, in which case coordinate names must be provided as bound variables. Examples include use with bvar elements and sample presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moment operator (moment, momentabout)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <moment/> element denotes the i-th moment of a data set or random variable. It accepts degree and momentabout qualifiers. If degree is absent, first order moment is assumed; degree should contain a single child when present. momentabout, if present, denotes the point about which the moment is taken; otherwise moment about zero is assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show degree=3 and momentabout mean applied to a list of data, and using moment with a variable X and a specified momentabout ci p. Sample presentations illustrate notation ⟨(...)^3⟩_mean and ⟨X^3⟩_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logarithm operator (log, logbase)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <log/> element represents the logarithm function relative to a given base. The optional <logbase/> qualifier specifies the base; if absent the base is assumed to be 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: <apply><log/><logbase><cn>3</cn></logbase><ci>x</ci></apply> (log_3 x) and <apply><log/><ci>x</ci></apply> (log x). Sample presentations include subscripted base when provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral operator (int) — definite and indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: The <int/> element is the operator element for a definite or indefinite integral over a function or a definite integral over an expression with a bound variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definite integrals indicated by providing qualifier elements specifying a domain of integration; lowlimit/uplimit pair is standard. Examples show ∫ sin = cos and ∫_a^b cos, and example with bvar x and lowlimit 0 uplimit 1 for ∫_0^1 x^2 dx. The int element can be used with bound variables serving as integration variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation operator (diff)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <diff/> element is the differentiation operator element for functions or expressions of a single variable. It may be applied to a function to denote its derivative or to an expression in a single variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bvar may contain a degree element specifying order of derivative. Examples: <apply><diff/><ci>f</ci></apply> (f') and using bvar x to express d(sin x)/dx = cos x; example of second derivative on x^4 with degree 2 in bvar is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial differentiation operator (partialdiff)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <partialdiff/> element is the partial differentiation operator for functions/expressions in several variables. For partial differentiation of a function, the containing partialdiff takes two arguments: a list of indices (positions of function arguments involved) and the actual function; indices may be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For algebraic expressions, bound variables are given by bvar children of the containing apply; bvar elements may contain degree elements specifying order of derivative in that variable. A top-level degree element without bvar indicates a total degree. Examples show partial derivatives with index lists and with bvar/degree annotations; sample presentations include multi-index D_{1,1,3}f and ∂^k f / ∂x^m ∂y^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic Constants (exponentiale, imaginaryi, notanumber, true, false, pi, eulergamma, infinity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict Content MathML rewrites to corresponding syntax table symbols. Examples demonstrate ln e = 1, i^2 = -1, 0/0 = NaN, logical mix-ins showing true ∨ P = true, false ∧ P = false, approximations π ≃ 22/7, γ ≃ 0.5772156649, and use of infinity symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set Theory Constants (integers, reals, rationals, naturalnumbers, complexes, primes, emptyset)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements represent standard number sets: <integers/>, <reals/>, <rationals/>, <naturalnumbers/> (including zero), <complexes/>, <primes/>, and <emptyset/>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show membership tests (42 ∈ Z, 44.997 ∈ R, 22/7 ∈ Q, 1729 ∈ N, 17+29 i ∈ C, 17 ∈ P, Z ≠ ∅). Presentation uses double-struck symbols (Z, R, Q, N, C, P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifiers (forall, exists)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <forall/> and <exists/> elements represent universal and existential quantifiers which take one or more bound variables and an argument specifying the assertion being quantified. Qualifiers such as condition or domainofapplication may be used to limit the domain of bound variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bind/forall with bvar x and assertion (x − x = 0) presenting as ∀x.(x−x=0). Existential examples show ∃x.(f(x)=0) and restricted existence like ∃x with domainofapplication integers yielding ∃x.(x∈Z ∧ f(x)=0). Strict MathML equivalents using csymbol for quantifiers and set membership shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lambda construct (<lambda>)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <lambda> element constructs a user-defined function from an expression, bound variables, and qualifiers. In an n-ary lambda, the first n children are bvar elements identifying placeholders; optional domainofapplication qualifier restricts the possible argument values. If lambda has no bound variables it's usually superfluous unless domainofapplication is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: λx. sin(x+1) or x ↦ sin(x+1). Notes about domainofapplication restricting functional arguments or being ignored if last child is not a function. Illustrates variants for representing function on integers via domainofapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interval element (<interval>)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <interval> element represents simple mathematical intervals of the real line. It takes an optional attribute closure with values open, closed, open-closed, closed-open (default closed). If interval immediately follows a bvar it acts as a qualifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show closures and sample presentations for (x,1), [0,1], (0,1], [0,1). Reference to 4.3.3.1 Uses of domainofapplication, interval, condition, lowlimit, uplimit when used as qualifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits (<limit/>)
rubrics_metrics.description: The <limit/> element represents taking a limit of a sequence. The limit point is expressed by specifying a lowlimit and a bvar, or by specifying a condition on one or more bound variables. The approach direction is given as an argument limit in Strict Content MathML supplying direction specifiers both_sides, above, below (corresponding to tendsto type values all, above, below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how to specify limit point and direction; used to encode sequence limits with bound variables and qualifiers. (No long example in this chunk but description of direction specifiers and relation to tendsto element provided.)
